lines.text: Never play a voicemail from your own number.
Mine came at 11:52 PM. At the laundromat.
lines.say: Mine came at eleven fifty-two P.M. At the laundromat.

lines.text: My own voice whispered: Don't look in dryer nine.
I was alone. But dryer nine was spinning.
Nobody had put anything in it.
Then something thumped against the glass.
If it stops, don't open it. Walk out. Now.
The dryer stopped. The door swung open by itself.
Inside was my hoodie. The one I'm wearing.
In the round glass, my reflection didn't move.
It lifted a phone to its ear. And whispered.
That's when I knew who sends the voicemails.
So if your own number calls tonight, don't play it.
